significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: a model's “representational transition matches the true boundary condition” and anticipates the onset of extrapolation error or misplaced confidence, thereby fixing expectations across sweeps of multiple scientific regimes rather than merely showing that a concept is decodable. It establishes a behavioral phenomenon and an internal representational account, though not a causal mechanism; specifically, the boundary signal would explain and predict when a model switches from valid application of a law to “confident-but-wrong extrapolation,” a sharper result than generic uncertainty-under-shift findings such as Ovadia et al. (2019). The negative branch would rule out domain-boundary encoding as a general explanation or diagnostic in the studied model class, although it would not rule out inaccessible nonlinear encodings; true and false outcomes are nevertheless distinguishable through boundary location and error-onset coupling. Topic substitution would not retain this score: merely asking whether scientific mechanisms are represented omits the claim-specific ordering between an internal boundary transition and later behavioral failure.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “Domain-of-Validity Score,” aggregating “boundary-detectability, boundary-location accuracy, and error/boundary alignment,” plus the associated read-only boundary signal. It is ex ante insofar as the claim says this signal “predicts confident-but-wrong extrapolation,” giving auditors an opportunity to flag or gate a prediction before trusting it, rather than only explaining an error after occurrence. Although extraction must be repeated per model and law, the transferable conclusion is the predicted relation between boundary alignment and extrapolation failure, not a single fixed activation direction; the asserted scope spans foundation models and laws in chemistry, physics, biology, and materials, with downstream use by model auditors and deployers. Topic substitution would not justify this reach because the broad scientific-representation topic alone supplies neither this predictor nor an action window before an invalid extrapolation.
